observations: body L1-L12: the figure stands on the left of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the vertical circles ZLB and ZET (radius 86.4 pt each) and the ecliptic GTBA (radius 174.8 pt), arcs of circles fitted to the print; the arc EB of the circle of latitude (radius 118.8 pt), the arc EL of the parallel, straight, and the dot of the Moon at E (radius 1.9 pt); the dashed lines OZζ, ζEτ, ζLβ, Eβ, OBβ, OTτ and ατ, each fitted to its dashes and drawn dash by dash as printed. The lines meet in β within 0.2 pt, in O within 0.8 pt, in τ within 1.2 pt and in ζ within 1.7 pt; the tangent ζLβ passes 1.1 pt from L, and the arc ZLB begins 2 pt before Z. Near E the dashes of Eβ lie on the arc EB.

body L1-L12: the tangents at E and L to the vertical circles meet OZ produced in the same point ζ because ZE = ZL (p. 261, L36-L37), and ζE = ζL = R tg z. In the plane triangle ζτβ the exterior angle ζβα exceeds the interior angle ζτα by the angle τζβ: the plane angle at ζ, as said in L12-L13.
body L9: an acute-shaped mark prints between the l and the a of «laterum».

body L11, L17, L21, L28, L32: «Ptolemaei et al–Battānī» (L11) is not letter-spaced; its «al–Battānī» has a long dash (5.3 pt), as have «22–23» (L17, 5.4 pt), «al–Battānī» (L21, L32) and «ar–Raqqah» (L28).

body L14-L16: the angle at ζ, small, is R EL : ζL in the measure of the sines; ζL = tg ZL = tg z, and EL = sin β sin ang. long. : R (p. 259, L40), whence L16, as printed. The plane angle at ζ is the spherical angle BZT of p. 261, L12 (sin BZT = sin β sin ang. long. : sin z) multiplied by cos z. A speck prints above the t of «tg ZL» (L14).

body L17-L20: the words in brackets differ from those proposed on p. 261, L14-L16: there the variation is divided by the sine of the corrected zenith distance (the spherical angle, p. 261, L12), here multiplied by its cosine and divided by its sine (the plane angle at ζ, L16).
body L22: the dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 9.8 pt; a heavy bracket closes Schiaparelli's addition begun on p. 261, L28.
body L23: the dash after «s)» measures 9.6 pt, the hyphen of «27-36» 3.1 pt.

body L24-L31: Theon's obliquity is Ptolemy's, 23° 51′ 20″ (Almagest I, 12), and exceeds al-Battānī's 23° 35′ by 16′. At ar-Raqqah (latitude 36°) the Moon in Cancer at its northern limit (latitude 5°) has the declination 28° 35′ and culminates 7° 25′ from the zenith, «7° 1/2»; the parallax there, 60′ sin 7° 25′ = 7′ 45″ (7′ 50″ with 7° 30′), is «7′ 1/2 circiter», and 16′ of zenith distance change it by 60′ cos 7° 25′ sin 16′ = 16″,5. A heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition (L25). Nallino's addenda (Part I, p. LXXV) add to this note that al-Battānī removed the discrepancies arising from the different obliquity, assigning in his tables (Part II, p. 95-101) to each of Theon's climates another latitude, suited to the new obliquity.

body L32-L37: al-Battānī's warning is p. 82, L33-L36 («nec hae quantitates sunt ut quae per angulos et arcus deprehenduntur, ob varias causas in iis accidentes, licet facilius quam illae sumantur»); Theon's tables go by equinoctial hours (15° of hour angle) and by climates whose longest days differ by half an hour (p. 82, L28-L32). The dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 10.0 pt; a heavy bracket closes the addition.
body L38: the dash after «t)» measures 9.6 pt, the hyphen of «3-18» 3.4 pt; a speck prints to the left of the head.
body L39-L40: a heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition, which goes on to p. 263.
notes L1-L2: the nonagesimal, 90° from the ascendant, is the highest point of the ecliptic above the horizon, where the circle through the zenith and the pole of the ecliptic meets it.
